mcq.stem: Placing a WAF in front of a public web app primarily protects against:

choices.text: Common web exploits such as SQLi and XSS

mcq.explanation: WAFs inspect HTTP(S) and block many application-layer attacks.

mcq.stem: A screened subnet (DMZ) is used to:

choices.text: Host internet-facing services separated from internal networks

mcq.explanation: DMZs isolate public services so compromise is less likely to reach the intranet.

mcq.stem: Which cloud model gives the customer the MOST responsibility for OS patching?

choices.text: Fully managed FaaS with no OS access

mcq.explanation: In IaaS the customer typically manages the guest OS and above.

mcq.stem: Customer-managed encryption keys in a public cloud MOST improve:

choices.text: Control over who can decrypt cloud-stored data
Physical cage ownership of the provider

mcq.explanation: CMK/BYOK keeps cryptographic control with the customer organization.

mcq.stem: For enterprise Wi-Fi, WPA3-Enterprise with 802.1X is preferred over PSK because it:

choices.text: Uses per-user credentials and stronger authentication
Removes the need for certificates forever

mcq.explanation: Enterprise mode authenticates individuals/devices instead of one shared passphrase.

Host public DNS recursively for the internet

mcq.stem: An east-west firewall between app and database tiers supports:
mcq.explanation: Internal firewalls constrain lateral traffic between tiers.

mcq.stem: Which TWO are shared-responsibility concerns in SaaS?

choices.text: Customer data classification and sharing settings
Customer patching of the provider’s hypervisor
Customer replacement of the provider’s data-center generators

mcq.explanation: In SaaS, customers still own identities, permissions, and data governance.

mcq.stem: Disabling WPS on wireless APs mitigates:
mcq.explanation: WPS has historically been brute-forceable; disabling it hardens Wi-Fi.

mcq.stem: TLS inspection (SSL/TLS decryption) on a proxy requires careful handling of:

choices.text: Privacy, certificates, and exception lists for sensitive apps

mcq.explanation: Breaking TLS for inspection impacts privacy and can break cert-pinned apps.

mcq.stem: An air-gapped network is MOST appropriate when:

choices.text: Systems must have no direct connectivity to untrusted networks
Public Wi-Fi is the only path

mcq.explanation: Air gaps isolate high-value or OT systems from external reachability.

mcq.stem: Infrastructure as Code (IaC) security scanning helps catch:

choices.text: Misconfigurations before cloud resources are deployed

choices.text: Disable unused services and close unused ports
Permit password auth from the entire internet without MFA

mcq.explanation: Reducing services and patching are foundational hardening steps.

mcq.stem: CASB solutions are primarily used to:

choices.text: Visibly control and monitor sanctioned/unsanctioned cloud app usage

mcq.explanation: Cloud access security brokers enforce policy on cloud services.
